title: EFC — Observational Evidence for Energy Flow
description: Qualitative synthesis arguing that multiple cosmological observations—redshift-based expansion, CMB anisotropies, gravitational lensing, and galaxy-cluster energetics—are consistent with a hypothesis that energy flow shapes space-time. The piece highlights evidence across scales, from cosmic voids to dark-matter halo edges, and outlines observational fronts where the energy-flow picture could be further tested.

key_results.main_finding: Survey of existing observations indicates that redshift trends, CMB temperature variations, gravitational lensing, and cluster-scale energetics are qualitatively consistent with an energy-flow-driven shaping of space-time and structure formation.
parameters_tested: large-scale energy redistribution across low-density regions
datasets_used: X-ray and SZ measurements of galaxy clusters

kill_criteria: KC1: High-precision SNe Ia and BAO distance–redshift measurements jointly indicate no accelerated expansion or energy redistribution consistent with the proposed energy-flow interpretation across low-density regions.

KC2: CMB temperature and polarization data (including ISW cross-correlations with large-scale structure) are fully explained by standard ΛCDM initial conditions with no residuals requiring energy-flow-driven contributions to structure seeding or evolution.

KC3: Weak-lensing shear and convergence statistics across tomographic bins match GR+ΛCDM predictions without systematic residuals, eliminating the need for additional energy-flow-induced curvature effects.

KC4: X-ray and SZ observations of the intra-cluster medium show energy budgets, temperature profiles, and turbulence fully accounted for by gravitational infall/feedback alone, with no evidence of sustained non-gravitational energy flows.
KC5: Peculiar velocity fields in and around cosmic voids reveal no coherent inflow/outflow patterns beyond standard gravitational evacuation, contradicting the proposed balancing role of energy flow.
KC6: Observations of halo edges and dark matter–baryon interactions (e.g., rotation curves and halo profiles) show no stabilizing effects attributable to energy flow beyond conventional dynamics.
